name: Scopone
description: Scopone is a skilful Italian four-player partnership card game in which cards or sets of cards are captured from the table by playing cards of equal value. It is closely related to Scopa.

overview.description: Scopone is a skilful Italian four-player partnership card game in which cards or sets of cards are captured from the table by playing cards of equal value. It is closely related to Scopa.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Italy
Time Period: Early 1900s
Historical Development: The game evolved from traditional Italian card games (related to Scopa).
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game in Italy.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

setup.players: Four players in fixed partnerships; partners sit opposite each other. Play is anticlockwise.
setup.deck: Italian 40-card pack (Latin suits: swords, clubs, cups, coins). Ranks Re, Cavallo, Fante, 7–2, A. Can use standard 52-card pack with 10s, 9s and 8s removed.
setup.dealing: Dealer chosen at random; deal passes right after each hand. Deal three cards to each player (anticlockwise from dealer's right), two face down to table centre, three more to each, two more to centre, three more to each. Four table cards are turned face up. If three or all four table cards are kings, redeal.
setup.equipment: Italian 40-card deck or stripped 52-card deck; score sheet (optional).

rules.objective: Your partnership aims to score 11 or more points before the opponents by capturing cards from the table and winning scoring points (cards, coins, sette bello, prime, and sweeps).
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal: Each player receives nine cards; four cards are placed face up on the table.
2. Play: Player to dealer's right leads; turn passes anticlockwise. Each turn a player plays one card: it may capture one or more table cards of equal rank or whose capture values sum to the played card's value; if no capture, the card stays on the table. Single-card capture takes precedence over sum capture when both apply. Captures are optional; if the card can capture, the capture must be taken.
3. End of hand: The last player to make a capture takes any remaining table cards (this does not count as a sweep).
4. Scoring: Four points per deal (majority of cards, majority of coins, sette bello, best prime) plus one point per sweep (clearing the table with one play).
5. Winning: First team to reach 11 or more points at end of a hand wins; if both reach 11 in the same hand, higher score wins; if tied, play further hands.
keyRules: Capture by matching rank or by sum of table card values; single match takes precedence over sum
Sweep (scopa): one point when your play captures all table cards
Prime (primiera): best set of one card per suit using prime values (7=21, 6=18, A=16, 5–2, pictures=10)
Last capture takes remaining table cards; taking last cards never counts as a sweep

strategy.basic: Prioritise winning the 7 of coins (sette bello); avoid giving away sweeps; leave at least 11 on the table when you cannot sweep to make it harder for the next player.
strategy.intermediate: Establish anchors (e.g. a rank only your side can match) to set up whirlwinds; lead or leave cards of ranks you hold two or more of; track paired vs unpaired cards to plan the last trick.
strategy.advanced: Pair and unpair sevens to control the prime; coordinate with partner (e.g. play same rank after partner to consolidate); leave totals that the next player cannot match to force a card to the table for your side to capture.
tips: Winning a sweep leaves the table empty so the next player must play; chains of sweeps (whirlwinds) are powerful.
Leaving exactly 11 can put right-hand opponent in a bind.
Remember which cards are unpaired for the dealer's last-card strategy.

variations.name: Scopone Scientifico (10-card)
variations.description: Ten cards dealt to each player, none to the table. Some play that the dealer's team does score one point for a sweep if the dealer's last card captures all remaining table cards.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Override structure for deal size and table start is game-specific; documented for reference.

variations.name: Re bello
variations.description: The king of coins (re bello) awards an extra point to the team that captures it; five points per deal (plus sweeps) instead of four.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring bonus only; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Napola / Napoli
variations.description: Team capturing A-2-3 of coins in sequence scores points equal to the highest coin in that unbroken sequence (e.g. A-2-3-4-5-6 scores 6). Capturing all ten coins (Napoleone/Cappotto) wins the game outright.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant scoring and win condition; no standard overrides.

variations.name: Target score 21
variations.description: Some play to 21 points instead of 11, especially when using extra point variants.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Target score 21 is a common variant; override path depends on schema constants.

scoring.description: Four points per deal: majority of cards, majority of coins (denari), sette bello (7 of coins), best prime (primiera). One point per sweep (scopa). First team to 11 or more points wins.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach 11 or more points at the end of a hand wins; if both reach 11 in the same hand, the side with more points wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Scopone is a skilful Italian four-player partnership fishing game; capture cards by rank or sum, score for cards, coins, sette bello, prime and sweeps. First to 11 points wins.
